# [[1.0.0 P-54 — Abdin et al. 2024 — Phi-3 Technical Report]]

- **Authors**: Marah Abdin, Jyoti Aneja, Hany Awadalla, Ahmed Awadallah, Ammar Ahmad Awan, Nguyen Bach, Amit Bahree, Arash Bakhtiari, Jianmin Bao, Harkirat Behl, Sébastien Bubeck, Jianfeng Gao, Mojan Javaheripi, Piero Kauffmann, Yin Tat Lee, Yuanzhi Li, Liliang Ren, Gustavo de Rosa, Corby Rosset, Olli Saarikivi, Adil Salim, Masahiro Tanaka, Andrea Tupini, Praneetha Vaddamanu, Pengcheng Yin, Can Xu, Yifan Yang, Donghan Yu, Lu Yuan, Chenruidong Zhang, Jianwen Zhang, Yi Zhang, Yue Zhang, Xiren Zhou (Microsoft Research).
- **Venue / Year**: arXiv:2404.14219 (April 2024); subsequent Phi-3.5 update (August 2024).
- **URL**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.14219
- **Anchors**: PRIM-3 (Target Skeleton-First), PRIM-6 (Multi-Stage Build/Test Repair), PRIM-14 (Software-Archaeology Stage), PRIM-22 (Comprehension); cross-references the SLM-aware prompt preamble (`compiletime.SLMPromptContractPreamble`) and the Qwen-Coder-family lineage [[P-21]].

## 1. Core Contribution

The Phi-3 family demonstrates that **sub-4B parameters can rival 8B-13B open-weight models on reasoning, code, and chat benchmarks** when trained on a curated mix of heavily-filtered public web data and high-quality *synthetic data*:

1. **phi-3-mini** (3.8B parameters, trained on 3.3T tokens) reaches 69% on MMLU and 8.38 on MT-bench — matching Mixtral 8x7B and GPT-3.5 despite being small enough to deploy on a phone.
2. **phi-3-small** (7B, 4.8T tokens) reaches 75% MMLU; **phi-3-medium** (14B) reaches 78% MMLU and 8.9 on MT-bench.
3. The training recipe centers on a *Data Mix Aware curriculum*: aggressively filter public web data with quality classifiers, then augment with synthetic instruction / reasoning / code data generated by stronger teacher models.
4. **Long-context (128K) variants** use RoPE scaling and an extended-tokenizer to support Phi-3-mini-128K-instruct, validating the architectural choice that powers the IterativeNavigator's chunked re-indexing.

**SLM-aware relevance for MAgHARCM**: Phi-3 demonstrates that 3.8B–14B "phone-class" SLMs can match or exceed 7B-13B base models on code tasks when the prompt and decoding regime are SLM-tuned. This is exactly the regime MAgHARCM runs in (Qwen2.5-Coder 3B-7B, StarCoder2 3B-7B, Phi-3-mini 3.8B).

## 2. Application in MAgHARCM

- **PRIM-3 (Target Skeleton-First)** — Phi-3's synthetic-data recipe mirrors the skeleton-first translation strategy: scaffold the structure (function signatures, trait bounds, type signatures), then fill in method bodies. Phi-3-mini in particular performs well on "fill-in-the-blank" style tasks because its training corpus includes masked-completion patterns.
- **PRIM-6 (Multi-Stage Build/Test Repair)** — Phi-3's chat-format alignment (system / user / assistant tags) makes it an ideal target for the **repair-mode prompt template** (`TranslatorRepairPromptTemplate`); the model consistently respects structured output schemas and rarely emits preambles when the prompt uses `<|user|>...<|end|>` correctly.
- **PRIM-14 (Software-Archaeology Stage)** — Phi-3-mini-128K-instruct's 128K-token context window enables a whole-file archaeology pass on legacy modules up to ~80 KB of source, reducing the IterativeNavigator's re-indexing churn. This validates the existing `compiletime.IterativeContextBudgetBytes` ceiling of 4 KiB per fragment as a conservative default — Phi-3 can comfortably exceed it when the project corpus fits.
- **PRIM-22 (Four Phases Comprehension)** — Phi-3's "Data Mix Aware" curriculum implies that the four phases (model, search, comprehend, articulate) work best when each phase's prompt is *phase-specific*. The MAgHARCM `RenderPromptTemplate` already supports per-phase prompt variants; Phi-3 is the validation that this matters at SLM scale.
- **SLM Prompt Contract** — Phi-3's published "instruct" format (`<|system|>\n<|user|>\n<|assistant|>`) is the canonical reference for the `compiletime.SLMPromptContractPreamble` template. Qwen2.5-Coder [[P-21]] and StarCoder2 [[P-22]] both converge on a similar chat-template; Phi-3 is the *SLM baseline* that documents it explicitly.

## 3. Hop-1 References (papers cited by Abdin et al.)

- Brown et al. (2020) — GPT-3 / Language Models are Few-Shot Learners (foundational SLM scaling claim).
- Vaswani et al. (2017) — Attention Is All You Need (transformer architecture baseline).
- Su et al. (2021) — RoPE (rotary position embeddings used by Phi-3 for long context).
- Touvron et al. (2023) — LLaMA 2 (the architectural template Phi-3 inherits).
- Roziere et al. (2023) — Code Llama (referenced as instruction-tuned code baseline).
- Li et al. (2023) — StarCoder [[P-22]] in MAgHARCM lineage (decoder-only code LLM).
- Bai et al. (2023) — Qwen Technical Report (referenced as Qwen-Coder predecessor).
- Bubeck et al. (2023) — Sparks of Artificial General Intelligence (referenced for reasoning benchmarks).
- Hendrycks et al. (2021) — Measuring Coding Challenge Competence With APPS (cited as code benchmark).
- Liu et al. (2024) — Lost in the Middle [[P-53]] in MAgHARCM lineage (cited as long-context evidence).

## 4. Hop-2 References (papers-cited-by-hop-1)

- Kaplan et al. (2020) — Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models (the scaling hypothesis that Phi-3 partially refutes; cited by GPT-3 / Brown et al.).
- Hoffmann et al. (2022) — Chinchilla compute-optimal scaling (cited by LLaMA 2 for compute/parameter trade-off).
- Wang et al. (2023) — Self-Consistency [[P-52]] in MAgHARCM lineage (cited by Qwen technical report as a reasoning technique).
- Wei et al. (2022) — Chain-of-Thought Prompting (foundational; cited by Qwen).
- Liu et al. (2024) — Lost in the Middle [[P-53]] in MAgHARCM lineage (cited by StarCoder2 [[P-22]] for long-context trade-offs).
- Austin et al. (2021) — Program Synthesis with Large Language Models (foundational code benchmark, cited by HumanEval lineage).
- Chen et al. (2021) — Codex / Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code (HumanEval; foundational).
- Schulman et al. (2017) — PPO / Proximal Policy Optimization (foundational for RLHF; cited by LLaMA 2 for instruction-tuning).
- Ouyang et al. (2022) — Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback (InstructGPT; RLHF origin).

## 5. Backlinks

- **PRIM-3** (Target Skeleton-First): Phi-3-mini's synthetic-fill-in-the-blank training mirrors skeleton-then-fill.
- **PRIM-6** (Multi-Stage Build/Test Repair): chat-format alignment is ideal for structured repair prompts.
- **PRIM-14** (Software-Archaeology Stage): Phi-3-mini-128K enables whole-file archaeology on modules ≤80 KB.
- **PRIM-22** (Four Phases Comprehension): phase-specific prompts validated by Phi-3's data-mix-aware curriculum.
- **PRIM-24** (SOP-Anchored Role-Artifact Schema): `compiletime.SLMPromptContractPreamble` uses Phi-3's documented `<|system|>...<|user|>...<|assistant|>` format.
